title: Nearest Hospital Finder: Closest Hospitals
description: Find the nearest hospitals to a place or your location with the Nearest Hospital Finder — mapped from open data, ranked by distance. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, in unfamiliar country the finder answers in seconds which town holds the nearest hospital — the kind of fact worth knowing before it is ever needed.
quick_answer: The Nearest Hospital Finder maps the hospitals OpenStreetMap records around a place or your location, ranked by distance. Search or use your location, press find, and see the closest hospitals. In an emergency, call your local emergency number first — this finder is for planning and peace of mind.

Remote trips deserve a hospital answer in the plan. Note the nearest two towns with hospitals before the route goes quiet.
Distance to a hospital shapes real decisions about where ageing parents live. This makes the distance a number instead of an anxiety.
Organisers record the nearest hospital in the safety plan. The ranked list is that line of the document, sourced.
The nearest entry is the answer; the second and third are the strategy — a closed road or a full department sends you down the list, so the list exists before you need it.

If someone is seriously ill or injured now, call the emergency number (911 in the US, 999 in the UK, 112 across Europe) before opening any map. Ambulances navigate professionally; this finder informs people.

faq: Should I use this in an emergency?
Call your local emergency number first — 911, 999 or 112. Dispatchers send help and guide you. This finder is for preparation and orientation, and says so at the top of the page.
Why might a hospital be missing?
It may be unrecorded in OpenStreetMap, newly built, or recorded as a clinic rather than a hospital. Coverage is strong in towns and cities; remote areas are thinner — the pattern of all open data.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — search any place name instead.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Hospital names change with trusts and systems; official directories are the freshest name source.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No.
Does it show emergency departments?
Where the map data records emergency facilities, the entries reflect it — but the data is not a live directory of A&E status. The hospital's own listing decides.
Straight-line distance misleads across water or mountains.
True of every ranking on earth — the list order is the starting point; your route app refines the drive. Knowing the candidates is the step this page owns.
Clinics and urgent care?
Facilities recorded as clinics may appear depending on the record; the hospital category is the finder's design.
Outside the US and Europe?
The finder works wherever OpenStreetMap has hospital records — which is most of the populated world, at varying depth.
Children's hospitals?
Where the record distinguishes them, entries reflect it; paediatric emergencies still start with the emergency number, whose dispatchers route correctly.
Urgent care centres?
Recorded clinics may appear with their own labelling. For anything time-critical, the hospital with emergency services is the destination — confirm its status on official listings.
